root_cause.text: A whitespace-stripping loop in the caiaq driver's `init_card` function uses the bound `len < sizeof(card->id)` (where `sizeof(card->id)` is 16), allowing up to 16 characters to be written into a 16-byte local buffer, leaving no room for a null terminator; when all 16 characters are non-space, the null terminator is overwritten, and the non-null-terminated string later causes a stack out-of-bounds read in `copy_valid_id_string`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `len < sizeof(card->id)` to `len < sizeof(card->id) - 1`, explicitly reserving one byte for the null terminator. The CVE description and commit message detail that the off-by-one has been present since commit bafeee5b1f8d ("ALSA: snd_usb_caiaq: give better shortname") and leads to a KASAN stack-out-of-bounds in `copy_valid_id_string`.
